title: Learning chords and harmony on his own
summary: After hearing of a visiting saxophonist who cut everyone running chords, he studies his father's harmony book and was writing orchestrations at fourteen.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: But I would listen to the guys talk about different things. And I heard them talk about a fellow who came from Milwaukee named Davani(?), a saxophone player, and they were talking about how he had, um, what in those times they called cutting everybody's head, you know, like a saxophone battle or that type of thing -- they called it a cuttin' session during those days. He had come through Jackson and cut everybody playing chord style; you know, running the chords. Most these guys might lay on a few licks, or a guy had a big sound or something, but this guy could move on the instrument. So I heard that, and I said, 'Well, I have to learn something about chords.' So I got some books, and I started reading about ...(?)., checking out the chords.

In the meantime, my father had left an Olerum(?) Harmony Book, which was a standard harmony book -- he left it on the piano. And I started reading this book. That's how I learned about harmony. I studied from this book all on my own, just bringing it down as best I could, you know. And actually, by watching and listening, I could orchestrate
for that orchestra... You know, by the time I turned fourteen, I could write orchestrations for that ...(?)..., just by, you know, listening to the guys and seeing what they talked about.
And that's the way... Most of my training was that way. I just taught myself.
Oh yeah. I did... The first one that came out right, where all the notes were right, I was 14 years old.

Oh, well, I didn't really pursue it. To this day I don't really pursue it. But I just wanted to know about it, you know. But I had the occasion to write some things later on, and I've been writing a little bit here and a little bit there ever since.
